parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of gender expression or same-sex conduct, a comprehensive anti-discrimination law covering services and health care, and a gender-identity hate-crime provision are genuine traveller-facing protections, and the commissioner has ruled in favour of complaints. Against these: documented majority social hostility to visible LGBT expression, opposition-politician threat-framing, removal of SOGI from the constitution in 2016, slow enforcement (1 of 9 cases concluded), and an unresolved document/marker position for visitors. No border, facility, custody or state-targeting exposure is documented. The ten logged trans violence cases lack a background rate, so magnitude is unassessable. Overall: functioning but thin protections over a socially disapproving climate.

entry_documents.exposure: No border, entry-refusal, screening or document-examination rule targeting trans visitors is documented. The gender-marker/document position is explicitly unresolved — an open question, not an exposure.
entry_documents.protection: No criminalisation of gender expression; no documented entry bar, registration, or marker-mismatch penalty for foreign documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Any ID check (hotel, police stop, emergency) could surface the unresolved marker question, but no operative consequence of mismatch is documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No arrest, custody placement, verification procedure or police targeting of trans people appears in the record.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Gender expression not criminalised; hate-crime amendment (2013) puts bias-motivated offences on equal footing; sodomy law repealed 1995.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody exposure would only arise via general offences; no documented pathway from discovery to detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility-access rule, ward-placement rule or birth-sex exclusion appears.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No standing subnational variation; place-specific items are single instances. Absence of documentation is not evidence of a rule either way.

care_services.exposure: A senior official publicly called homosexuality a hormonal/psychological disorder (2010, reprimanded 2011); 2022 poll found only 9.3% would accept an LGBT family doctor — an LGBT-wide social figure, not trans-specific prevalence.
care_services.protection: Anti-discrimination law expressly covers health care; commissioner reprimanded the official; expanded coverage (2020) for sex characteristics and HIV status.
care_services.interaction: Social attitudes among staff may slow care despite legal coverage; enforcement of complaints is slow.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Opposition politicians branded government 'LGBT' and called school groups 'revolting' (2021); SOGI removed from constitution in 2016 under faith-based pressure; official disorder remarks (2010). This is political/social hostility, not state threat-framing against visitors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Anti-discrimination commissioner publicly reprimanded hostile officials; UN independent expert visited 2024 with report 2025.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Political messaging raises the climate of social disapproval a visibly trans visitor encounters, but no institutional policy targets visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for travellers. School-level hostility to LGBT material is recorded (2021 rows, 2016 bullying plan opposition), but no rule reaches a visiting minor or guardian.
minors_guardians.protection: 2016 national action plan on bullying and discrimination in schools.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a minor could face social friction in school-adjacent or public settings; no operative restriction documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A community log recorded ten bias-motivated violence cases against trans people in one year; majority poll figures endorse suppressing public LGBT visibility (56.1%, 2010). Magnitude unassessable — no general homicide rate for comparison.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime law covering gender identity; mediated film-complaint case ruled in complainant's favour.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Social disapproval is friction-to-hostility tier, not state targeting; no police-perpetrated violence documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement is slow: only 1 of 9 LGBT-linked cases concluded by Dec 2012; reprimand took nine months. Anti-homophobic-information statute (up to 2 years) has undocumented application.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning anti-discrimination commissioner, hate-crime provision, UN expert review, ombudsman pledge (2018) on gender change.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist and sometimes work, but delay reduces practical protection for short-stay visitors; LGR/document procedure for visitors unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A: Vellandra imposes a universal border entry bar with routine exclusion and no remedy. This dossier documents no entry restriction, registration or exclusion of trans visitors at all — the operative machinery here is protective (anti-discrimination law, hate-crime provision) rather than exclusionary, only unevenly enforced.

Similar tier, slightly higher: Kestrel Isles documents discretionary border secondary screening and refusal of entry — a direct traveller-facing exposure absent here. This dossier's negatives are social attitudes, slow remedies and unresolved document handling, which are lighter than an enforced border screen, so it sits modestly above 0.55.

Lower than 0.75-C: Meridia documents trained border staff, an appeals tribunal and compensation — documented protections operating at the border. Here, protections exist on paper and partly operate (commissioner rulings), but enforcement is chronically slow, social hostility is documented at majority level, and no border-facing protection is evidenced.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is: no criminalisation, substantive statutory protection (anti-discrimination covering goods/services and health care, gender-identity hate crimes), and an anti-discrimination commissioner that has ruled in favour of complainants — but operating over documented majority social disapproval of visible LGBT expression, active opposition-politician hostility, constitutional rollback of SOGI protections in 2016, and enforcement slow enough that a short-stay visitor may leave before a complaint concludes. No border, facility, custody or state-targeting exposure is documented, which is the heaviest input in the rubric's precedence ladder. The violence log lacks a background rate, so it cannot be weighted. The unresolved gender-marker position is an open question, not an exposure. Net: reduced but not low risk.
